name: Temple Towns of the Kaveri Delta
theme: The living temple-towns of the Chola heartland along the Kaveri — from Thanjavur's Big Temple to island Srirangam, with Shiva, Vishnu and Murugan shrines between
region: Kaveri delta (Thanjavur, Thiruvarur & Tiruchirapalli), Tamil Nadu
description: The Kaveri, the great river of the Tamil south, spreads into a green delta that was the heartland of the Chola empire — and no stretch of India is more densely woven with living temples. This circuit follows the river through its temple-towns. It begins with the imperial Chola statements in stone: Brihadeeswarar at Thanjavur, the thousand-year-old Big Temple, and its echo at Gangaikonda Cholapuram, with the jewel-like Airavatesvara at Darasuram nearby — together the UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples — and the late Chola Kampahareswarar at Tribhuvanam. Around Kumbakonam, where Sarangapani descends from Vaikuntha in a stone chariot, gather Adi Kumbeswarar; Swamimalai, where Murugan became his father's teacher; and Thirunageswaram, with Oppiliappan beside it. Thiruvidaimarudur and Thiruvaiyaru keep Shiva's worship alive on the riverbank; Thiruvarur remembers the cradle of Carnatic music; Thanjavur's Thanjai Mamani Koil honours Vishnu; and at the delta's head Srirangam and Thiruvanaikaval share an island — Vishnu reclining in the largest living temple on earth, and Shiva as the water element.
